source: FLEURS dev transcripts, through bournemouth_aligner's std G2P
note: Aspirated (ʰ) and breathy-voiced (ʱ) stops are tokens of their own; the puff or murmur after the release belongs to the stop, not to the vowel. bʰ and bʱ both occur for the same letter; treat them alike. Dental (t̪ d̪ n̪) and retroflex (ʈ ɖ ɳ) consonants are different tokens; plain t and d almost never occur.

SIL.name: silence
SIL.plain: A pause: no speech. Use it for a pause the speaker makes inside a segment.

noise.name: noise
noise.plain: A non-speech sound: a breath, cough, laugh or click.

<unk>.name: unknown
<unk>.plain: The G2P wrote a sound this model has no token for. Keep its time span; the label cannot say what it is.

s.name: voiceless alveolar fricative
examples: s ɔ h i t̪ ɔ
ɛ n ɛ s w e

i.name: close front unrounded vowel
examples: n̪ i ŋ ɡ ʌ ɭ

e.name: close-mid front unrounded vowel
e.plain: e as in Spanish or Italian “de”; the start of English “say”
examples: ʋ e ʋ e r ɯ

n.name: alveolar nasal
examples: ɛ n ɛ s w e

l.name: alveolar lateral approximant
examples: k ɔ r i t̪ʰ i l e
s l a l o m

o.name: close-mid back rounded vowel
o.plain: o as in Spanish or Italian “no”

r.name: alveolar trill
examples: bʱ a b ɔ r e
n u m b ɛ r

m.name: bilabial nasal
examples: m ʌ ʈ ɾ ɯ m

d.name: voiced alveolar stop
examples: t̪ ä p w ɾ ɪ d d̪ʱ i
ɾ ɑ d d͡ʑ ɨ j ʌ t̪ ɨ n

ɾ.name: alveolar tap
ɾ.plain: one quick flap of the tongue, as in Spanish “pero”. Also used for ɾ̪, which this model has no token of its own for
examples: m ʌ ʈ ɾ ɯ m
p ɾ ɔ t̪ʰ ɔ m ɔ

j.name: palatal approximant
j.plain: y as in “yes”. Also used for jᵊ, which this model has no token of its own for
examples: p ɯ d̪ ɨ j a

b.name: voiced bilabial stop
examples: ʔ e m b ʌ d̪ ɯ

ɛ.name: open-mid front unrounded vowel
examples: ɛ n h ɛ k a
ɛ n ɛ s w e

w.name: labial-velar approximant
examples: ɛ n ɛ s w e

ɡ.name: voiced velar stop
examples: n̪ i ŋ ɡ ʌ ɭ

z.name: voiced alveolar fricative
examples: z j ä d̪ ä t̪ ə ɾ

ʔ.name: glottal stop
ʔ.plain: the catch in the throat in “uh-oh”

ŋ.name: velar nasal
examples: n̪ i ŋ ɡ ʌ ɭ

ɯ.name: close back unrounded vowel
examples: m ʌ ʈ ɾ ɯ m

ɐ.name: near-open central vowel
ɐ.plain: a short, relaxed “uh” (Portuguese “cama”, German “-er” endings). Rare: not in the test sentences of any trained language

q.name: voiceless uvular stop
q.plain: a k made further back, at the uvula (Uzbek “q”). Rare: not in the test sentences of any trained language

ʂ.name: voiceless retroflex fricative
ʂ.plain: a hard sh with the tongue tip back (Polish “sz”)
examples: ʂ u ʈ ʌ ɾ s

ɣ.name: voiced velar fricative
ɣ.plain: a g where the tongue does not close (Dutch g, Spanish g between vowels)

ɨ.name: close central unrounded vowel
ɨ.plain: between ee and oo, lips spread (Polish “y”, Welsh “u”)

ɕ.name: voiceless alveolo-palatal fricative
ɕ.plain: a soft sh, with the tongue body raised (Polish “ś”)

ɳ.name: retroflex nasal
ɳ.plain: n with the tongue tip curled back

ɲ.name: palatal nasal
examples: p ɔ ɲ t͡ʃ ɔ m ɔ
ʋ ɨ ɲ ɑ n ɨ ɡ ʌ ɭ

ʉ.name: close central rounded vowel
ʉ.plain: a rounded vowel between ee and oo (Norwegian and Swedish “du”). Rare: not in the test sentences of any trained language

ʈ.name: voiceless retroflex stop
ʈ.plain: t with the tongue tip curled back (Swedish and Norwegian “rt”)
examples: m ʌ ʈ ɾ ɯ m
t͡ʃʰ ʊ ʈ ʈ i j õ

t͡ʃ.name: voiceless postalveolar affricate
examples: s u t͡ʃ ɔ n a

t͡ɕ.name: voiceless alveolo-palatal affricate
t͡ɕ.plain: a soft ch (Polish “ć”, Bosnian “ć”). Rare: not in the test sentences of any trained language

t̪.name: voiceless alveolar stop, dental
t̪.plain: t as in “ten”; dental: the tongue tip touches the upper teeth
examples: s ɔ h i t̪ ɔ
m ʌ t̪ ɨ j a

ɭ.name: retroflex lateral approximant
ɭ.plain: l with the tongue tip curled back

ɔ̃.name: open-mid back rounded vowel, nasalised
ɔ̃.plain: o as in British “thought”; nasalised: air also flows through the nose (French “an”, Portuguese “não”)
examples: p ɔ h ɔ̃ r i b a

õ.name: close-mid back rounded vowel, nasalised
õ.plain: o as in Spanish or Italian “no”; nasalised: air also flows through the nose (French “an”, Portuguese “não”)

kʰ.name: voiceless velar stop, aspirated
kʰ.plain: k as in “key”; aspirated: followed by a puff of breath before the vowel starts (English “top” has one, “stop” does not)

ɖ.name: voiced retroflex stop
ɖ.plain: d with the tongue tip curled back (Swedish and Norwegian “rd”)
examples: ʔ ʌ ɖ ɨ p ʌ ɖ ʌ ɪ̯ j ɑ ɡ ʌ k

ʌ.name: open-mid back unrounded vowel
examples: m ʌ ʈ ɾ ɯ m

ʋ.name: labiodental approximant
ʋ.plain: a soft v without friction (Dutch w, Slovenian v)
examples: m ɨ ɡ ʌ ʋ ɯ m

pʰ.name: voiceless bilabial stop, aspirated
pʰ.plain: p as in “pen”; aspirated: followed by a puff of breath before the vowel starts (English “top” has one, “stop” does not)
examples: pʰ ɔ l̪ a pʰ ɔ l̪ ɔ

k̚.name: voiceless velar stop, unreleased
k̚.plain: k as in “key”; unreleased: a final stop with no audible burst: the closure is held and the sound ends silently

d̪.name: voiced alveolar stop, dental
d̪.plain: d as in “dog”; dental: the tongue tip touches the upper teeth

ẽ.name: close-mid front unrounded vowel, nasalised
ẽ.plain: e as in Spanish or Italian “de”; the start of English “say”; nasalised: air also flows through the nose (French “an”, Portuguese “não”)

ɦ.name: voiced glottal fricative
ɦ.plain: a breathy, voiced h (Dutch and Czech h)

ɛ̃.name: open-mid front unrounded vowel, nasalised
ɛ̃.plain: e as in “bed”; nasalised: air also flows through the nose (French “an”, Portuguese “não”)

n̪.name: alveolar nasal, dental
n̪.plain: n; dental: the tongue tip touches the upper teeth

t͡ɕʰ.name: voiceless alveolo-palatal affricate, aspirated
t͡ɕʰ.plain: a soft ch (Polish “ć”, Bosnian “ć”); aspirated: followed by a puff of breath before the vowel starts (English “top” has one, “stop” does not). Rare: not in the test sentences of any trained language

t̚.name: voiceless alveolar stop, unreleased
t̚.plain: t as in “ten”; unreleased: a final stop with no audible burst: the closure is held and the sound ends silently

ã.name: open front unrounded vowel, nasalised
ã.plain: a as in Spanish “casa”; nasalised: air also flows through the nose (French “an”, Portuguese “não”). Also used for ä̃, which this model has no token of its own for

l̪.name: alveolar lateral approximant, dental
l̪.plain: l as in “leaf”; dental: the tongue tip touches the upper teeth
examples: ʔ ʌ l̪ ʌ d̪ ɯ
d͡ʒ e t̪ e b e l̪ e

ä.name: open front unrounded vowel, centralised
ä.plain: a as in Spanish “casa”; centralised: said closer to the centre of the mouth than the plain vowel

p̚.name: voiceless bilabial stop, unreleased
p̚.plain: p as in “pen”; unreleased: a final stop with no audible burst: the closure is held and the sound ends silently
examples: ʈ ɪ p̚ p ə ɳ i

ɽ.name: retroflex flap
ɽ.plain: a flap with the tongue tip curled back
examples: ɡ u ɽ i k ɔ

s̪.name: voiceless alveolar fricative, dental
s̪.plain: s; dental: the tongue tip touches the upper teeth

í.name: close front unrounded vowel, accent ´ (high)
í.plain: ee as in “see”; accent ´ (high): the G2P's dictionary marks a pitch accent or stress here. Rare: not in the test sentences of any trained language

r̩.name: alveolar trill, syllabic
r̩.plain: a rolled r; syllabic: forms a syllable with no vowel, as the n of “button”. Rare: not in the test sentences of any trained language

ĩ.name: close front unrounded vowel, nasalised
ĩ.plain: ee as in “see”; nasalised: air also flows through the nose (French “an”, Portuguese “não”)

ɐ̃.name: near-open central vowel, nasalised
ɐ̃.plain: a short, relaxed “uh” (Portuguese “cama”, German “-er” endings); nasalised: air also flows through the nose (French “an”, Portuguese “não”). Rare: not in the test sentences of any trained language

t͡ʃʰ.name: voiceless postalveolar affricate, aspirated
t͡ʃʰ.plain: ch as in “church”; aspirated: followed by a puff of breath before the vowel starts (English “top” has one, “stop” does not)

ʊ̃.name: near-close back rounded vowel, nasalised
ʊ̃.plain: oo as in “book”; nasalised: air also flows through the nose (French “an”, Portuguese “não”)

ɪ̯.name: near-close front unrounded vowel, non-syllabic
ɪ̯.plain: i as in “sit”; non-syllabic: the weak, glide-like half of a diphthong; it is not a syllable on its own

ə̃.name: mid central vowel (schwa), nasalised
ə̃.plain: the weak vowel of “about”, “sofa”; nasalised: air also flows through the nose (French “an”, Portuguese “não”)

t̪ʰ.name: voiceless alveolar stop, dental, aspirated
t̪ʰ.plain: t as in “ten”; dental: the tongue tip touches the upper teeth; aspirated: followed by a puff of breath before the vowel starts (English “top” has one, “stop” does not)

ɻ.name: retroflex approximant
ɻ.plain: an English-like r with the tongue tip curled back
examples: p ʌ ɻ ʌ ɪ̯ j a

ũ.name: close back rounded vowel, nasalised
ũ.plain: oo as in “food”; nasalised: air also flows through the nose (French “an”, Portuguese “não”)

d̪ʱ.name: voiced alveolar stop, dental, breathy-voiced
d̪ʱ.plain: d as in “dog”; dental: the tongue tip touches the upper teeth; breathy-voiced: voiced, then released with a breathy, murmured puff (Hindi “bh”, “gh”)

bʱ.name: voiced bilabial stop, breathy-voiced
bʱ.plain: b as in “bed”; breathy-voiced: voiced, then released with a breathy, murmured puff (Hindi “bh”, “gh”)
examples: bʱ a b ɔ r e

ʈʰ.name: voiceless retroflex stop, aspirated
ʈʰ.plain: t with the tongue tip curled back (Swedish and Norwegian “rt”); aspirated: followed by a puff of breath before the vowel starts (English “top” has one, “stop” does not)
examples: s ɔ b u ʈʰ a r u

bʰ.name: voiced bilabial stop, aspirated
bʰ.plain: b as in “bed”; aspirated: followed by a puff of breath before the vowel starts (English “top” has one, “stop” does not)
examples: a ɾ ɔ m bʰ ɔ

ú.name: close back rounded vowel, accent ´ (high)
ú.plain: oo as in “food”; accent ´ (high): the G2P's dictionary marks a pitch accent or stress here. Rare: not in the test sentences of any trained language

ɪ̃.name: near-close front unrounded vowel, nasalised
ɪ̃.plain: i as in “sit”; nasalised: air also flows through the nose (French “an”, Portuguese “não”)

ɡʱ.name: voiced velar stop, breathy-voiced
ɡʱ.plain: g as in “go”; breathy-voiced: voiced, then released with a breathy, murmured puff (Hindi “bh”, “gh”)
examples: d̪ u r ɡʱ ɔ ʈ ɔ ɳ a

ɡʰ.name: voiced velar stop, aspirated
ɡʰ.plain: g as in “go”; aspirated: followed by a puff of breath before the vowel starts (English “top” has one, “stop” does not)

d͡ʒʱ.name: voiced postalveolar affricate, breathy-voiced
d͡ʒʱ.plain: j as in “judge”; breathy-voiced: voiced, then released with a breathy, murmured puff (Hindi “bh”, “gh”)

ɖʱ.name: voiced retroflex stop, breathy-voiced
ɖʱ.plain: d with the tongue tip curled back (Swedish and Norwegian “rd”); breathy-voiced: voiced, then released with a breathy, murmured puff (Hindi “bh”, “gh”)
examples: b ɔ ɖʱ u t̪ʰ i b a

ɽʱ.name: retroflex flap, breathy-voiced
ɽʱ.plain: a flap with the tongue tip curled back; breathy-voiced: voiced, then released with a breathy, murmured puff (Hindi “bh”, “gh”)
examples: l ɔ ɽʱ e i ɾ ɔ
